projects.content:
_Need to generally be ambiguous about the work. Hard to talk numbers_


# General Context


Sure Inc., focuses on building a platform that allows companies to own the entire insurance flow from choosing products to sell, generating documents, configuring pricing, triggering emails, etc. It’s a entirely configurable system.


## My Pod


The team I worked for built and maintained core features including documents, emails, webhooks, and pricing calculations (ROC). 🐬 


_maybe a graphic handling a lot of general structure_


A lot of engineers on my team really prided themselves on strong integration / unit testing and deep code reviews which really suited my engineering philosophies.


However, my team had to interface with several other teams including a group responsible for a solid component library.


## My Contributions


Unfortunately, due to restructuring I only worked on this team / division for about 6 months. But I made significant contributions to every domain except ROC. Additional work focused on refactoring existing code and adding QA automation tests.


## Documents


The UI underwent a fairly large refactor / improvement. Originally, the document hub was a rudimentary system with a simple UI. We added a lot of new functionality including

- Document contextual state management to handle save states across multiple components
- Document reordering built using React DnD’
- Document test mode that programmatically pulled variables and input options
- Improved error handling for a ton of backend validation edge cases
- Better trigger system that could handle file, section, or document generation conditions

## Emails / Webhooks


Simple work adding additional options for triggering emails and webhooks, but focused on refactoring a lot of hardcoded code for reusability.

projects.title: Porfolio
projects.description: Fully static site built entirely during GitHub workflows using React Router 7 framework. Leverages Notion for CMS project management and Claude for intelligent palette generation.
projects.content:
# It’s just a static website


At its core, yes, this is a static website. _Periodt_. 


But, underneath that, it has a lot more work put into it:

- Notion database as a makeshift CMS for managing project content
    - Automatic PR’s and CI on cron schedules when Notion databases are updated
- GitHub workflows to handle CI checks, GitHub Page Deployments, and Cron Jobs
    - E2E, Unit, and Linting to keep code clean and reusable and check for breaking changes in an age of Agentic coding
    - Sentry Error Logging and Monitoring
- Intelligent palette creation using Claude prompts in a workflow to generate swappable website color palettes based off project images

Frontend engineering is a lot more than just writing HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; though admittedly I love that part of the field, it’s a constantly evolving space.


## 💾 Notion Database


Leveraging Notion as a headless CMS requires a paid plan to access the Notion API. After receiving an API key, you can query individual databases and loop through rows and items.


![Portfolio Notion Database Setup](/images/content/porfolio/porfolio-0.jpeg)

- `Doc Name` - Corresponds to project title _(subject to change, honestly)_
- `Tags` - Added as project tags, just for extra knowledge / SEO perhaps, but might be useful for querying and sorting in the future
- `Favorites` - Boolean checkbox primarily used for generating specific palette themes
- `Description` - Project description on projects page
- `Color` - Theme color for the individual project page right up (like this one)

### Automatic PR and CI on Notion Changes


I [configured a cron job](https://github.com/deeplyfriedchicken/kevincunanan/blob/main/.github/workflows/fetch-notion.yml#L5) to run nightly which hits the Notion API and checks for changes. 


IF it detects changes, it’ll overwrite a JSON file and open a PR. GitHub is set for automatic merging as well, so this _should_ all run automatically without me needing to configure anything.


![image.png](/images/content/porfolio/porfolio-1.png)


## 🔬 GitHub workflows to handle CI/CD


Every push to main must be handled through a branch + PR. Pull requests can only get merged if CI checks pass. Once a PR is merged to main, we kick off a workflow to deploy to GitHub Pages.


![CI/CD workflow](/images/content/porfolio/porfolio-2.jpg)


## Testing & Linting

> quote on AI and importance of testing software

LLM’s and agents are quickly becoming an important part of the software engineering space. Anyone who’s not using the tools here is going to fall behind. However, the somewhat unsupervised nature of code means that testing has become more important. 


### Unit & E2E Tests


Basic strategies for unit and e2e happy path testing were implemented. The most important things to test are the Notion scripts and Project components and flows handling data.


### Linting


Linting checks run after completed agent task runs and on PR’s.


### Sentry


To monitor errors and failed jobs, I’ve added Sentry to the Notion data fetching scripts. My future feature is to add monitoring and dashboards for errors and general metrics.


We also added Sentry React to handle 404 errors, but hopefully I’ll catch and handle more errors in the future.


## 🎨 AI Generated Color Palettes


Attached to the `fetch-notion` workflow is a color palette generator. Introducing the `Favorites` property;  using AI, if there’s any projects with cover icons with that boolean property enabled, we feed Claude the logo and ask it to produce a color-accessible color palette.


![Fetch Notion + Claude Palette Workflow](/images/content/porfolio/porfolio-3.jpg)


I built a flexible theme picker using Tailwind and a `data-theme` property. These were static color palettes that were decided in Figma. However, I personally felt these lacked character and purpose in general. 


It’s a fun way to use AI and the Notion CMS together without creating a big risk for prompt injection on my site.
